item.title: Re: additional idea information
item.content:encoded:
Really, the 400 word limit exists for a reason. There's no explicit rule about adding onto the original post with a reply, but frankly, that is because it should be common sense not to do so.

Speaking as a reviewer and forum crit staff, the word limit is there to make our lives easier, but I think it can be beneficial to the author, too. When writing an SCP, you are essentially writing a story, forced into a specific format. I think the ideas template can be your first experience with this idea of restriction. It helps you think about your idea in all different aspects aside from what makes it good, which can help you identify flaws. Moreover to the point, the word limit can serve as a gauge for how much you understand an idea.

It's not an exaggeration to say that every single article on the site can be summarized in 400 words or less. It ultimately depends on how you choose to summarize it. Focusing on important aspects, such as structure, narrative, emotion, and so on, while ignoring extraneous details is the best way of summarizing an idea. A reviewer won't care whether your SCP is blue or red, they'll care about the story you're trying to tell, and how you're trying to tell it. Having the ability to summarize your idea in a limited wordspace displays a good understanding of your concept. Believe me when I say that 400 words is actually very generous, in the grand scheme of things.

TL;DR, don't try to artificially decrease word count, save space by booting extraneous details and semantics, make reviewers happy. Good luck!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Ahoy there, pvm08. Greetings and welcome to the SCP Wiki!

My name is Hexick, and I'm a Junior Staff member on the site's CO team, and a (sometimes) author. Since you're interested in becoming an author on the Wiki, I highly recommend you go about reading through some of the newer articles available to get a feel for what types of content the community is currently interested in. I personally suggest checking out SCP-5057. Not only that, but if you're interested in talking with members of the community to become acquainted, it would be a good idea to go about joining our IRC chatrooms. Anyway, here are some resources to help you get started:

◎ Open Resources ◎
◉ Close Resources ◉

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

With that said, I hope you enjoy your time here, and if you have any questions or concerns, feel free to contact myself or another member of CO Staff via Wikidot or IRC.

item.title: Re: any suggestions to make my SCP look better?
item.content:encoded:
Feedback
Read Below

A couple things here:

The entire page should be looked over for punctuation errors. Capitalization, commas, etc. It breaks immersion seeing a Foundation researcher write;

"by singing the song take on me by aha"

It should be:

"By singing the song Take On Me by Aha."

Revision 5159-A should be capitalized, and I highly recommend it is put in a quote box to separate it from the rest of the page.

- Audio from Skimmers radio during investigation

You should add who Skimmers is, before the log. I don't know if he is a government agent, an MTF officer, a scientist, etc. Example:

MTF Agent dispatched: Skimmers, John
Time: 0500 Dec 16, 2020
Reason for dispatch: Unknown anomalous presence

This gives more clarity on who he is. Remember, the Foundation documents basically everything. They are trying to study these things, and these documents are looked back upon for research in the future.

Interviewer: do you have a name?

SCP-5159: Yes, my name is Joseph Walker.

Here personally I don't think the Foundation really cares what his name is. They view him as an anomaly, not as a person. Staff are often very cold with the SCPs unless there is an anomalous or memetic reason not to be.

Also don't forget your rating module. A common mistake.

Other than that, good job.

item.title: A Physically-Impossible Restraining Order
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard Format, Testing Logs.

Elevator Pitch:
- A document that may be used to physically restrain someone
- If used, Person B would not be able to enter the distance provided by Person A for the stated amount of time.
- Person B is physically impended by an invisible barrier.

Central Narrative:
The central narrative would be told over the testing logs, a baseline test to see how it works before certain "interesting" tests are done, the story here would be subtle in the notes afterwards, subjects reporting feeling safer after a certain death, etc.
Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The testing logs will include what I believe to be unique testing logs, like what would happen if someone put their name in for both options, what would happen if the distance was set at a giant amount, etc.
Additional Notes:
If people feel the story might not be clear just via notes of the testing logs, I might also include a discovery log which gives more hints (since I'd rather it not be obvious).

item.title: Re: Memetic Conversation Cards
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Let's see what we have here…

A set of ever-changing anomalous conversation cards that compel the reader to do whatever the card has written on it- for example, if one said "read this card over and over", the subject would be forced to read the card over and over until the cards are taken from them or they expire.

Mind-affecting objects have been done before, but that doesn't mean you can't put another spin on it. let's see the narrative shall we?

A group of researchers testing the capabilities of the SCP after MTF recovery units with memetic resistance read the cards and are forced to do the actions on the cards, requiring a second team to come in. They are located in a house with a family who is also stuck performing the acts described by the cards. The researchers have extensive testing logs in which they test the capabilities of the cards, ending in a scenario where the last card says "Cause a containment breach at Site-██. " The result box says nothing but [DATA EXPUNGED] resulting in ██ casualties. Testing on SCP-XXXX halted indefinitely.

Okay, this seems kinda boring. So it's only purpose in the narrative is to cause a attainment breach at the end. I mean, the card idea is kinda interesting, depending vastly on what the cards show. I also feel like the last;

ending in a scenario where the last card says "Cause a containment breach at Site-██. " The result box says nothing but [DATA EXPUNGED] resulting in ██ casualties. Testing on SCP-XXXX halted indefinitely.

is kinda pointless. I personally don't see why they would have any Foundation personnel using this mind-affecting item, instead per say, a D-Class. I also doubt a D-Class could do much damage.

Although the SCP seems harmless to the researchers at first, the cards in the testing log become more and more malicious as time goes on.

I still don't understand why researchers would use themselves as subjects to the cards in the first place. Even if they did, once testing started to become more malicious I feel like D-Class would come in anyways.

The cards then convey a message to the researchers, ending in something like I KNOW YOU'RE READING THIS : GET AWAY FROM MY CARDS : [EXPLETIVE REMOVED] YOU : Cause a containment breach at Site-██.

Are the cards sapient? If so, why do they do what they do? Are they one entity? Is someone controlling them? Why do the cards exist? If they're just here to make people go crazy and do harmful actions, I just find that boring. Unless you have narrative of course.

Overall Thoughts: "Overall, this has some substance and little to no narrative. First, I suggest you think more about this idea overall. It needs more. So far this is just a thing that does a thing for no reason. That's fine I guess, but very boring. Narrative is what drives a story forward. So, what is the narrative? Did someone create the cards? Are the cards someone? Maybe the cards are an entity's eyes? Also, why are the cards basically evil? Do they have any reason to be? Once you answer these questions, I believe you can go somewhere with this idea. Hope your concept gets better man. PM me if you need help with the concept.

- Close

item.title: Re: Another Day for the (Logistics Department)
item.content:encoded:
Hiya. Disclaimer: I am not authorized to give greenlights. please reach out to more experienced users for more informed crit.

To summarize, I think this is a (potentially) good premise, and a bad pitch.

The summary you've laid out is really just a basic thriller set-up. Everyman dude has a thing, bad things happen, dude has to get from point A to point B with the thing. This is the elemental premise of most western action-thrillers, so it doesn't give me any insight into the potential appeal of such a tale. With such a basic plot structure, the reader will most likely not be taken in by the premise alone, and so you're going to have to rely on other elements of your writing toolbox to generate interest.

That being said, having a common plot structure is not at all a bad thing! Execution is everything. It's just that it's hard for me to tell from the info you've provided what the angle of that execution is. Will Gabriel's character development invest the reader? Does the unknown anomaly have fascinating or confusing effects that will warp the story in an interesting way? Is there a conspiracy going on with the GOI that sets up some chilling world-building opportunities?

It's not that this idea can't or won't work, it's just that the info you've provided doesn't sell me.

Have a good day!


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Another Day for the (Logistics Department)

I like the play on the honey panacea scam and the funk. Monteparnas seems to be saying the gravestone/coffin transportation is a Chekhov's gun situation, but I disagree. The ending of the story clearly reveals one mysterious way in which the bodies are sourced. I also like that this is not 100% doom and gloom, since the effects are seemingly positive and these entities may be content immortals enjoying a benign afterlife/second life. There's still that menace/sickening factor in the cannibalistic element though, which gives it an appropriate SCP flavor.

One tweak I'd humbly recommend since Dr Calder described a similar issue: when the log starts, I was a bit thrown off by the names. It may just be me, but it seemed at first like the agents were listening in on a conversation in the house due to the casual tone and use of pronouns. Shortly after, I realized the two speakers were the agents, but it briefly took me out of the article. Maybe put Agent in front of their names or something like that? It would also help fix the issue Dr Calder had with similar names.

I'll +1 anyway, just some thoughts.

item.title: Re: The Perpetual Lawnmower
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit

Let's do this…

SCP-XXXX is a lawnmower that perpetually gets faster and doesn't suffer from wind resistance or interact with physical objects, until it comes into contact with grass. When it touches grass it becomes 'real' and suffers the effects of wind resistance from the speed that it is going.

Okay, right off the bat, this sounds uninteresting. It's a thing that does a thing.

This is an anomaly created by a new POI, who created this specifically to mow their lawn for them without any effort. This SCP was found moving away from this POI's place of residence at very high speeds, allowing the foundation to get a rough idea to where this POI lives.

The narrative sounds rather boring too. That being said… A new POI sounds interesting to me. Maybe a guy that's super lazy and makes anomalies to do work for him? That's an idea.

Its a dangerous lawnmower that moves super fast.

That's doesn't sound like a hook, that's just restating what the anomaly is.

Overall Thoughts: I believe you need more time to thing about a proper narrative. Your anomaly is very simple and that's okay, but no one will want to read it if they're is no narrative. I hope your idea goes somewhere man. Remember, you do you.

item.title: Re: Idea Critique: Staff conflicted morals on a anomalous site.
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

The premise is about an anomalous village filled with people (SCP-XXXX-1 or -1s) that are generally harmless inside, but if they get out they could be dangerous (how they are dangerous is to be determined, but not world-ending - maybe just dangerous to the civilian populace). The staff are instructed to not sympathize, but are not told what will happen if they do.

Okay, there is very little detail for me to go on. So many questions. How are they dangerous? Civilian Populace? Is the whole village filled with the -1s or are they accompanied with regular people. If so, do the people know about the -1s or have the -1s stayed secret for this long. Why are the staff instructed not to sympathize? Does it have something to do with their anomaly? What is their anomaly? If you want Foundation Personnel to sympathize with the -1s, you're gonna have to try damn hard, because we're used to killing civilians and feeding people to monsters on a daily basis.

The catch and twist of the story is how the staff fight each other from the ones who want to let the -1s out, and the ones who want to keep them contained. There will probably be a separate tale about both sides of the conflict if this is greenlighted.

This doesn't sound like a catch or twist. If anything it sounds damn right confusing. The Foundation is cold. If there was people sympathizing with the -1s, they would be transferred, given amnesics, or something else of the sort. You also want to make a separate tale about this? That's cool, but first you MUST focus on making this happen first. Otherwise the tale can't happen.

Basically about conflicting morals for foundation staff, and who is the "bad guy" - letting the -1s out, or keeping them contained.

This conflict has been done before. You're gonna need to either sharpen the narrative so it stands out or come up with something more unique.

Overall Thoughts: You need to edit this thing. You have little substance, an idea of a narrative, and not much else. The moral has been done before, but that doesn't mean you can't do it. So overall, do a few more thinking sessions and figure it out. It sounds like you have something in mind, but have done poorly to explain it. I hope your idea becomes reality. Remember, Excelsior!

- Close

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello there, Dr Szabo. Welcome to the SCP Wiki!

Glad to see you're interested in writing for the Wiki. I'm Hexick, and I'm a Junior Staff member on the Community Outreach Team, along with several others. When getting into writing for the site, it's usually a good idea to read around a bit to gauge what the community is interested in. I personally suggest checking out SCP-5858. Anyway, here are some resources to help you out around the site as you enter in to your creative endeavor:

◎ Open Resources ◎
◉ Close Resources ◉

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

An ancient interdimensional gateway with an unknown origin located somewhere in Antarctica's underground, which leads to a world where lies a cosmic entity. However, with the mind of a kind-hearted average joe.

item.title: Re: The Evolves (Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Okay, let's cope with this.

Has normal teenager appearances. He is the first person to have been spotted with such abilities. Hacks into the foundation database almost everyday in hope to find someone like him (the foundation is close to developing a software to protect their database). Isn't really cooperative due to being separated from his parents and knows that he will never be able to see them. Hobbies include singing, reading fictional books.

It sounds like your putting WAY too much attention into the character then the narrative you're attempting to tell, if you are attempting to create one. So far, you've only told me about this new generation (with little detail), slapped me in the face with this character, then told me said character has abilities. (Details like his hobbies aren't exactly necessary by the way. It's fine if you add them, but if they have little impact on narrative or the item themselves, you should probably leave it out.)

Besides the common ability mentioned above. These "Evolves" have a unique ability. "The First" I want this article on has the unique ability to engineer a virus which attacks on the human brain and shuts it down in 2-3 days. When an infected is in contact with any computer, the virus will inject some of its code which will act as a computer virus capable of taking down the entire NASA Database in a single day.

Okay, more ability stuff. So you're saying he's so powerful he can take down any computer system really? That sounds really OP, but not interesting. I still want to hear about the narrative you're trying to tell.

I want this article on has the unique ability to engineer a virus which attacks on the human brain and shuts it down in 2-3 days.

Why? Also, if this is so, I doubt the Foundation would just interact with the kid too much then.

Overview: Okay, this has little to no narrative. That's the main problem. The second problem is how the foundation interacts with him. You make it sound like he has his own room and they just keep an eye on him.

Hacks into the foundation database almost everyday in hope to find someone like him (the foundation is close to developing a software to protect their database).

The Foundation WOULD NOT let anyone do this. If he's in the Foundation's system, they are going to force him out. Sure, they're developing a software to go against him, but why waste resources on that when I can just isolate him from all tech. He can infect people you say? I don't see why they can't work around that.

So, just a refresh. I would like to hear more details about the narrative, less about the character, and for the Foundation to not sound like they're a hotel service. They're all about Secure, Contain, Protect, not: Service, Comply, and Party.

You can always PM me if you need another review after the aforementioned stuff is figured out. I wish you the best of luck my man.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Mystery

Page Layout: Standard SCP article.

Elevator Pitch: SCP is a 4k HDTV with a standard TV remote. When you switch the input to HDMI-1 you can see a POV of a random person in the world. Changing the channel would change the POV to another random individual.

Central Narrative: The article would explore several unique circumstances, like a POV of someone dying, someone who needs glasses, someone tripping on hallucinogens, someone dreaming, someone with color-blindness, etcetera.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The chances of you finding your own POV out of 7 billion people would be virtually impossible. So I'd describe a process where SCP scientists use several d-class's to keep flipping through channels until they come across somebody who worked for the SCP foundation. They'd be found and then asked to stare in front of the TV. What happens is essentially they'd be staring at an infinite mirror, the user of this circumstance would enter into a trance and would require a third party to get them away from the TV. The person in question would eventually wake up and explain what exactly they felt.

Additional Notes: What kind of feelings would they experience? Nirvana? Dread? Would they want to immediately kill themselves? I know that's kind of played out but I want to make sure I hit all the beats.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: Portal Tunnel System
item.content:encoded:
Hello! Not an official reviewer, but here's my thoughts.

+ Crit
- Uncrit

This seems like another "thing that does a thing" and very bare bones - something that would've worked in Series I, but not now. Why should I care about this parallel universe?

Central Narrative: Advanced humans from this universe built the system long ago to enter the alternate universe. The humans were successful in entering, and returned to this universe centuries later.

Okay, and? Why did the advanced humans from another universe want to enter our universe? Where are they now? Why should the audience care about them?

The Foundation looks for an entrance, finds one, and enters.

How does the Foundation know there's an entrance? Why do they want to go through it?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The history of the alternate humans, and the pantheon of gods they worship, all with there own history.

First off, it's their, not there. Also, why are the gods these alternate humans worship relevant to the SCP at hand? The other problem with this is that the hook is supposed to be what is unique about your premise, but I already mentioned the problem with this.

I'd suggest you rely on logs of people exploring the alternate universe, but you have to make something about the alternate universe stand out, since this concept has been done before. Maybe elaborate on the questions I asked earlier.

Overall, I think if you could find a way to make this stand out, it would be a really good SCP.

item.title: concept idea!
item.content:encoded:
Basically this SCP is a suit of armor and it transforms to whatever the armor of the era it is in. So for example if it is put on in our current era it will transform into basic combat armor. When it is not being worn it turns into Spartan armor. The effects of it are as follows, the SCP will have a telepathic sort of call sort of like a voice in your head pulling you towards it. The SCP also grants the wearer invincibility other worldly strength and great skill in combat (all forms of combat including strategy like organizing wars and things along that line). The catch is if it is not worn by a highly trained individual that also has great amounts of will the armor will drive the wearer insane and cause the wearer to enter a blood rage killing everything in its path and after a certain period of time (no longer than a few hours) the subject will die. The idea behind that is the armor slowly sucks away the human wearing it so it retains their knowledge but kills the body. If worn by highly trained individuals the blood rage does not happen and the body deteriorating takes much longer (unknown amount of time).

I had ideas for a proper narrative about its origins but I could not figure out how the foundation would know any of this information. My basic original idea was that during the battle of Thermopylae when Leonidas was killed a Persian took and wore his armor causing the spirit of Leonidas to set a curse on it causing the effects we see in the armor, following this theme I had ideas for the armor to appear throughout history and effect many famous soldiers throughout history causing their success and eventually their deaths. As for other parts of this story I basically wrote on how the foundation tests the armor using D-class personnel and then eventually allows and MTF soldier to test the armor which goes well until the soldier returns later in the day to retrieve the armor and it quickly killed by guards as he was incredibly hostile as if he needed the armor for his own survival.

As for containment measures or reasons that this item is kept by the Foundation I thought that the basic containment measures are it needs to be kept away from any other SCP that effect personnel mentally or any humanoid SCP that could put on the armor. And then as for reasons the Foundation contains it is because first of the obvious threat it posses especially if another SCP gets to it and also I had the idea for it to be allowed use in the case of world ending events or very large site containment breaches. Any feedback would be greatly appreciated!

item.title: Re: A tale about the foundation’s attempts to deal with spies within the foundation
item.content:encoded:
I like this idea! The premise of the Foundation dealing with spies isn't really unheard of, but it's rare enough that it would deserve a tale of its own.

+ Here's my main questions
- Do with this what you will

1) Will this be like sort of "short episodic tales?" Since we're dealing with multiple GOI's, individual chapters or tales of such could be easier to digest and read than one big tale, but having a deep exploration of this topic could captivate readers a lot more. This is entirely up to you!

2) Who would be the main culprit of infiltration? The Foundation has a lot of enemies; which of them would likely have spies already in the Foundation? For this reason, the Chaos Insurgency seems to be the primary suspect. That's not to say that other groups can't be the main suspect.

3) If there is an A story and a B story, would they be different tales, or will they be put together in alternating chapters? The A story centering inside the Foundation could be a seperate tale with chapters featuring different GOI spies and the B story could be fundamentally the same, except without a central figure.

4) Lastly, will the story escalate involving anomalies and SCPs, or will the Foundation keep this under wraps? This is a question for the future really, but this concept really is intriguing.

+ Critique?
- Critique...

I get the idea and the concept is not really explored in detail (from what I can remember). My main concern is how will you write and execute it. Will this tale be ended quickly, or be endless? What else could you do with the concept of spies in the Foundation? There is lot that can be done here, but what would be done?
Do with this what you will!

And that's all I have for you! Again, I really like this idea and this idea deserves a tale of its own. Good luck with your SCP! :D
